title: Northern Mariana Islands Long-Term Legal Residents Relief Act
sponsor: Del. Sablan, Gregorio Kilili Camacho [D-MP-At Large]
official_summary:
Northern Mariana Islands Long-Term Legal Residents Relief Act

This bill grants Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands (CNMI) Resident status to certain aliens who have resided continuously and lawfully in the CNMI since November 28, 2009. An individual with such status shall be (1) authorized to work in the CNMI; (2) issued travel documentation; and (3) inadmissible to the United States at any port of entry outside of the CNMI, with the exception of Guam in certain instances.

To qualify for CNMI Resident status, an alien must meet various requirements, such as having (1) been lawfully present in the CNMI on the date of this bill's enactment or on December 31, 2018; and (2) resided continuously and lawfully in CNMI from November 28, 2009, through this bill's enactment.

summary.headline: This law gives certain long-term legal residents of the Northern Mariana Islands a special CNMI Resident status that allows work and travel documents in the islands.
summary.what_it_does: The law creates CNMI Resident status for certain non-citizens who have lived lawfully and continuously in the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands since November 28, 2009. People with this status may work in the CNMI and receive travel documents. They cannot enter the United States at ports of entry outside the CNMI, except in certain cases involving Guam.

who_it_affects.group: Non-citizens who have lived lawfully in the CNMI since November 28, 2009
who_it_affects.how: They may qualify for CNMI Resident status if they meet the law's residence and lawful-presence requirements, which allows them to work in the CNMI and receive travel documents.

who_it_affects.group: Non-citizens who qualify for CNMI Resident status and travel outside the islands
who_it_affects.how: They are barred from entering the United States at ports of entry outside the CNMI, with an exception for Guam in certain instances.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted June 25, 2019, and the qualification rules refer to that date; the summary does not describe a separate effective date.
